A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaSCALE. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable matching despite reformatting, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original CIFAR and ImageNet OOD-detection experiments, including sensitivity, robustness, ablation, and latency results.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds LINe comparisons, ViT-B-16 sensitivity results, and score-distribution analyses.

M1.justification: Both retain the same perturbation procedure, activation-shift statistic Q, correction term, eCDF-controlled percentile, and AdaSCALE-A/L variants. Expanded explanations and revised latency wording do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The CIFAR and ImageNet datasets and near-OOD, far-OOD, full-spectrum, corruption, and adversarial-model scenarios remain unchanged. New sensitivity studies and distribution plots use already represented datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: v3 Table 14 adds LINe to the ImageNet-1k/ResNet-50 comparison containing NNGuide and MDS in v2 Table 13. The expanded ATS discussion does not include newly evaluated ATS results.

E3.justification: v3 Appendix E introduces ViT-B-16 individual-parameter sweeps and a joint epsilon, lambda, o, and pmax grid evaluated using validation AUROC. The retained benchmark metrics, training settings, and final model-specific percentile settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Adds ViT-B-16 sensitivity analyses in Tables 19–20 and RegNet-Y-16 score-separation diagnostics in Appendix K. Existing ResNet sensitivity, Q/Q' ablations, corruption, adversarial-training, and ISH analyses remain; several are merely relocated.

E5.justification: Both report three independent CIFAR training trials, the same mean and standard-deviation display in Figure 2, and 10,000 latency trials. No new seed information, uncertainty intervals, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark tables retain their numerical results. v3 adds LINe scores, ViT sensitivity results, and Figure 6 distributions, and corrects Figure 3's reported Q' ratio ordering from greater to smaller. Figure 6 reports SCALE/ImageNet-O AUROC 76.84, versus 76.43 in the retained RegNet-Y-16 table (v2 Table 36; v3 Table 39), without explaining different settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, eCDF construction, adaptive-scaling equations, and Appendix D.1 toy calculations remain substantively unchanged. Separately numbering existing formulas adds no theory; Figure 3's inequality correction concerns a reported empirical observation.

C1.justification: Both retain the adaptive-scaling contribution, state-of-the-art performance claims, minimal ID-data requirement, and generalization with one tuned hyperparameter. The conclusion's stronger 'principled footing' wording does not introduce a new substantive scientific claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation that OptFS can distort informative original logits on near-OOD inputs and expands the complementary-signal rationale. Its revised latency discussion says random perturbation avoids the additional forward pass, conflicting with Appendix D.3's two-pass description and the retained activation-shift computation.

D1.justification: v3 removes v2's code-availability statement and repository link without replacement access instructions. It documents ViT sweep grids and clarifies one-time OpenOOD hyperparameter selection. The link removal establishes reduced in-paper access information, not that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Adds LINe (Ahn et al., 2023) to related work and references, and expands comparisons with ATS regarding forward passes, eCDF use, and data requirements. Discussion of differences from OptFS also expands; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Includes localized rewrites and expanded explanations in Sections 4.1 and 5.2, reordered discussion topics, relocation of the Q' ablation discussion to Appendix D.2, and replacement of Broader Impacts with a generic Impact Statement. The main narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from one to two columns, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures and tables. Robustness and FSOOD tables are reorganized, existing Q/Q' averages are redisplayed, and sensitivity tables and Figure 6 are added. Figures 1–5 retain their original graphics.

improvement.justification: The added ViT sensitivity evidence, LINe comparison, and corrected Figure 3 description improve support and clarity. However, v3 removes code-access information and introduces an inconsistent forward-pass explanation and unexplained differences between Figure 6 and Table 39 AUROCs. These benefits coexist with reproducibility and reporting regressions, leaving the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
